items.title: Charles Leclerc on journalist ban: “I was surprised by the choice of words”
items.summary: Charles Leclerc had no hand in getting a veteran Formula 1 reporter barred from the paddock, and he isn't interested in policing the press - even when the headlines get a little personal.

items.title: Rafael Camara torn between his F2 title bid and more F1 races with Haas
items.summary: Rafael Camara is torn between completing his title-contending Formula 2 campaign and seeing out the 2026 season at Haas in Formula 1. The Ferrari protege is the reigning F3 champion and leads the F2 standings as a rookie with Invicta Racing, courtesy of a starring campaign in which he has taken five pole positions and seven feature race podiums including three victories.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton: "You can't be the only one pushing for change" in F1
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he had hoped others in Formula 1 would follow his lead in speaking out on issues around the world, but admitted that "so far that's not the case". The seven-time world champion has used his platform for causes including diversity in motorsport and, more recently, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

items.title: Honda reveals key F1 power unit change for 2027
items.summary: Immediately after the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, Honda was still unable to fully explain Lance Stroll's DNF. The Canadian was forced to retire for the 14th time, equalling the all-time record for the most retirements in a single Formula 1 season.

items.title: Isack Hadjar stunned as his most expensive trading card sells for five-figure sum
items.summary: Red Bull Formula 1 driver Isack Hadjar was left speechless when Topps revealed how much the most valuable of his trading cards had sold for. The card company filmed the Frenchman being shown an autographed card carrying three Red Bull patches and asked him to put a price on it. He recognised it straight away, but his first guess was some way off. "I remember signing this one.

items.title: Isack Hadjar reveals why he cannot follow Max Verstappen into racing outside F1
items.summary: Red Bull Formula 1 driver Isack Hadjar says he would love to race in other categories during the off-season, but admits he does not "have enough money" to do so yet. Several of Hadjar's rivals already race outside grands prix.

items.title: Max Verstappen on F1's WHOOP plan: "It's nobody's business, I don't even know my heart rate"
items.summary: Ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Formula 1 announced a partnership with WHOOP. A number of drivers will wear the company's health trackers, with their data being shown live during TV broadcasts in 2027. The latter, however, remains entirely optional, leaving the decision up to the drivers themselves.

items.title: Charles Leclerc brands Brazil penalty for Liam Lawson contact "a bit harsh"
items.summary: Ferrari Formula 1 driver Charles Leclerc has branded his five-second penalty that cost him seventh place at the Brazilian Grand Prix as "harsh", arguing that his contact with Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson was "part of racing". The Monegasque driver tapped the left rear of Lawson's Racing Bulls car at Turn 12 on the penultimate lap at Interlagos, before passing him five corners later.

items.title: Charles Leclerc reveals the gadget he’s been "hiding" in his Ferrari
items.summary: Charles Leclerc has revealed that he has already been wearing a WHOOP fitness tracker while driving his Ferrari, and says he has "nothing to hide" as Formula 1 prepares to put drivers' heart rates on screen. F1 announced on Wednesday that WHOOP will become an official partner of F1, with drivers wearing its wristbands in the car.

items.title: Red Bull F1 e-bike in Max Verstappen's Suzuka livery hits the Las Vegas Strip
items.summary: Red Bull fans in Las Vegas this weekend can ride home on a piece of Max Verstappen's 2025 season, with the team's official e-bike going on sale at a pop-up shop on the Strip. Californian electric bike brand SUPER73 is selling its limited-edition Oracle Red Bull Racing models at the Podium Collective, a free pop-up hosted by Julien Solomita's Bad Year Racing at the Bellagio.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli: Yo-yo racing to return at F1 Las Vegas GP
items.summary: Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli has predicted the return of “yo-yo” racing at this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix thanks to its low-downforce characteristics. The new-for-2026 regulations, which feature a more electrical power unit, have caused a radically different style of racing at certain circuits with it being labelled as ‘yo-yo’.

items.title: Max Verstappen: "If they let me write the rules, F1 wouldn’t be allowed in certain places"
items.summary: Although the FIA's announcement was only online for five minutes, there is no doubt in the paddock that V8 engines will return to Formula 1. An agreement in principle has been reached on a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 with a smaller electrical component, which is set to be introduced in 2030 rather than 2031.

items.title: Liam Lawson had little doubt he would remain for F1 2027 amid Nikola Tsolov talk
items.summary: Liam Lawson has confirmed he had little doubt that he would remain on the Formula 1 grid for 2027 after recently extending his Racing Bulls contract. The 24-year-old and rookie team-mate Arvid Lindblad were announced last Thursday as the Italian outfit’s driver pairing for next season following a very strong 2026.

items.title: "Disappointed" and "no excuses" – Oliver Bearman frustrated by lack of 2027 F1 contract
items.summary: Following confirmation that Liam Lawson and Valtteri Bottas will remain on the grid, only one seat formally remains vacant for the 2027 Formula 1 season. It is the Haas seat currently occupied by Oliver Bearman.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton on his card collection: "I'm 41 years old and I love Pokémon"
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton has admitted that his love of collecting Pokémon cards has survived well into his adult life after a trip to buy packs for the youngest members of his family turned into a car full of collectors.

items.title: Fernando Alonso rules out staying in F1 for V8 return: "16 years of pure racing lost"
items.summary: Although the FIA's formal confirmation on Tuesday was only online for a few minutes before being temporarily taken down again, it is clear to everyone in the paddock that V8 engines will return to Formula 1. The agreement in principle involves a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 – with the turbo being particularly important for Audi and Honda – and a significantly smaller electrical component.

items.title: Lando Norris names George Russell as F1's next James Bond
items.summary: Lando Norris thinks George Russell would be the Formula 1 driver best suited to play James Bond, and says the Mercedes driver would even give up racing for the role. The question came days after Amazon MGM Studios confirmed Robert Pattinson as the next actor to play the legendary British spy following a five-movie run from Daniel Craig.

items.title: LISA becomes first artist to design F1 clothing collection
items.summary: LISA has become the first artist to design a Formula 1 clothing range, with her 'Pretty Fast' collection going on sale around the world today. The Thai singer, who made her name in K-pop group BLACKPINK before going solo, designed the capsule with Ceremony of Roses, a creative agency that works on the commercial side of music artists' careers.

items.title: Lando Norris jokes he "found the limit of a champagne bottle" in Brazil podium mishap
items.summary: 2025 Formula 1 champion Lando Norris has joked about how he "found the limit of a champagne bottle" for the first time in his career during his chaotic podium celebrations at the Brazilian Grand Prix. The McLaren driver won from pole at Interlagos, but his trademark celebration went wrong. As he slammed the champagne bottle down on the floor, it shattered in his hands.

items.title: Lando Norris on "GTA VI": "I wasn't allowed to play it when I was younger"
items.summary: Lando Norris admits he won't be playing Grand Theft Auto VI during Formula 1's final triple-header of the season while also revealing that he wasn't allowed to play the popular franchise when he was a child.

items.title: LEGO reveals Speed Champions sets for all 2026 F1 drivers and teams
items.summary: Toy giant LEGO has announced it will produce all 2026 F1 cars and 22 drivers in minifigure form, as it hosts its latest exhibition race in Las Vegas. Off the back of its partnership first launched in 2025 and expanded this year, LEGO will introduce an entire range of F1 Speed Champions in March 2027, which means every single 2026 car and driver will be available to fans.

items.title: What the Valtteri Bottas contract renewal says about Cadillac's F1 future
items.summary: The longest-running contract saga of the Formula 1 season is now at an end. Not that it has been blockbuster material, since it revolves around a team struggling to lift itself from the back of the grid.

items.title: Valtteri Bottas beats Colton Herta to 2027 Cadillac F1 seat
items.summary: Incumbent Valtteri Bottas will remain with the Cadillac Formula 1 team through 2027 after the US-owned team decided against fast-tracking American test driver Colton Herta to a race seat. Bottas will stay on board with Cadillac alongside Sergio Perez as initially planned, with both race-winning veterans having signed a multi-year deal when they initially joined F1's 11th team.

items.title: F1 to showcase driver health data as it partners with WHOOP
items.summary: Formula 1 has signed a deal with wearables company WHOOP which will see a number of drivers wear the company's health trackers and showcase their data on the TV broadcasts in 2027. WHOOP will become an Official Partner of F1 in a deal that will see an increasing number of drivers start wearing tech bracelets provided by the company while inside the car.

items.title: Five things to watch out for at the F1 Las Vegas GP
items.summary: Formula 1 kickstarts its final triple-header of the 2026 campaign with this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix. The American venue serves as race 21 of the 23-round calendar with grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi to follow Vegas and round out the year.

items.title: Future imperfect: What's behind the abortive 2030 F1 rules announcement?
items.summary: Famously, when the papal conclave gathers to elect a new pope, a successful vote is communicated to the huddled masses via smoke from the Sistine Chapel chimney as the chemically impregnated ballot papers are burned: white smoke signifies a decision, black means yet another round of voting.

items.title: Speed, trust, controlled aggression - What really led to Liam Lawson's career-saving F1 2026
items.summary: Liam Lawson's improved form made him too good for Racing Bulls to ignore for the 2027 Formula 1 campaign. But, as always, there's more than just a single factor behind that upturn in performances.

items.title: The Kimi Antonelli you don't know, told by those closest to him
items.summary: There is one thing that physiotherapist Sergi Avila took a little while to understand. When Kimi Antonelli finally found himself with a free weekend, after weeks being spent between circuits, airports and training, the most logical choice would have been to stay at home: sleep a few extra hours, meet friends and switch off.

items.title: Oscar Piastri set for grid penalty at F1 Las Vegas GP
items.summary: McLaren driver Oscar Piastri is set for a 10-place grid drop at Formula 1's Las Vegas GP for exceeding his engine allowance for the season. Piastri was already on the limit of four internal combustion engines for the year but will need a fifth Mercedes V6 engine to finish the 2026 campaign.

items.title: Toto Wolff details subdued Mercedes F1 celebrations after securing 2026 double
items.summary: Mercedes officially completed its return to the top of Formula 1 at the chaotic 2026 São Paulo Grand Prix, successfully locking down the constructors' world championship one week after Kimi Antonelli secured the drivers' title. But for team principal and CEO Toto Wolff, the historic milestone was not met with an explosive nightclub celebration in Brazil.
